sections.heading: Expanding Your Business to India: Legal and Business Considerations
paragraphs: Expansion into a new country is a big step. Usually you're seeing fresh opportunities or customer growth or a market that makes good business sense. For many foreign companies, India is one of those markets. But before opening an office or hiring a local team, there's one important decision to make how should you establish your business legally?

This is the point at which an Indian subsidiary registration becomes an important option. This means that the foreign company can set up a separate legal entity in India, but it will be linked to the parent company. This is chosen by many businesses because it is adaptable, helps build a local network and is easier to manage under Indian laws.

The registration process can be confusing and complex, particularly if you are not familiar with the corporate laws of India. We understand at Services Plus. In this guide, we will look at what an Indian subsidiary is, who can register, what documents you will need, the registration process and some practical points that every business should know before they start.

Say an organization from the USA, UK, Singapore or another country wants to do normal business in India. It may set up a company here, which will be governed by Indian laws but will be owned or controlled by the foreign parent company, instead of running everything from abroad. That is how an Indian subsidiary company is.

Usually the parent company owns more than 50% of the shares and so it controls how the business is run. The subsidiary is also a separate legal entity at the same time. It may enter into contracts, employ staff, open bank accounts, pay taxes and conduct business activities in India in its name.

This is the reason why Indian subsidiary company registration has become the preferred choice of many international businesses planning for long-term growth. A registered subsidiary, whether it is selling goods or providing services or establishing a subsidiary business in India, makes for a stronger and reliable business presence.

Not all foreign companies come to India for the same reason. Some want total control of their operations; some want to work with a local partner. That’s why there are different types of business structures.

This option is suitable for foreign companies that want to have full ownership of their Indian business; thus, Indian subsidiary registration is the most feasible way. This enables the parent to operate independently under the Indian rules and regulations.
An Indian company enters into a joint venture with a foreign company. Ownership, responsibilities and resources are shared between both parties according to the terms agreed upon.

A liaison office is mainly used for communication and building relationships. It can act as the parent company’s representative in India but cannot undertake any commercial or revenue-generating activities.
A foreign company can do certain business activities in India through a branch office. But it is within the permissions allowed under Indian regulations.
In India, such an office is generally set up for a particular project.” The office is typically closed following completion of the project unless further approval is secured.

If the business is aiming for the long term growth and if you are planning to set up a subsidiary company registration in India, knowing these structures beforehand can help you to choose the one that suits your business goals.

Each company has its own reason to come in to the Indian market. Some want to reach more customers; some want to establish a long-term presence. An Indian subsidiary gives businesses the ability to do so while operating as a legally registered company.
Here are some of the biggest advantages:
